author: high
claim: Let \(p\) be a prime and let \(G\) be a finite group of order \(p^n\) for some integer \(n\ge 1\). Prove that the order of the center \(Z(G)\) is divisible by \(p\), and hence that \(Z(G)\) contains a nonidentity element.

verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. It uses the conjugation action and the orbit-stabilizer theorem to show that every non-singleton conjugacy orbit has order divisible by p, identifies singleton orbits with elements of Z(G), and applies the resulting class equation to conclude that p divides |Z(G)|. Since the identity lies in Z(G), this divisibility implies |Z(G)| is at least p and hence Z(G) contains a nonidentity element.
